# zfls

> zfls is a Fortran language server written in Zig: one native program for Linux, macOS and Windows that gives an editor completion, hover, definitions, references, rename, diagnostics and formatting for Fortran, runs a compiler's checks, builds a file to run, and has a debug adapter (`zfls dap`). It is a port of fortls and takes fortls's command line options and configuration files.

## Using it (for an agent setting it up)

1. Get zfls: a release of https://github.com/cesiumlang/zfls (one program, nothing else to install), the installation scripts in `packaging/`, or the VS Code extension `cesiumlang.zfls`, which includes it.
2. Start it from the editor's language client as `zfls`; it speaks the Language Server Protocol on standard input and output. `zfls dap` is the debug adapter, `zfls --help` lists the options.
3. Put a project's options in `.zflsrc` (TOML) at its root; `zfls config` prints each option in effect and where it came from.
4. Each diagnostic has a code; `diagnostic_severity` in `.zflsrc` or a `! zfls: disable=CODE` comment turns one off.

Each page is also served as Markdown, at the paths below.

- [Overview](index.md): what zfls is, getting it

Getting started:

- [Installing](installing.md): release archives, installation scripts, the macOS package, verifying a download

- [Configuration](configuration.md): `.zflsrc`, the user's file, settings over LSP, precedence

Reference:

- [Features](features.md): everything zfls does
- [Compilers](compilers.md): what works with gfortran, ifx, ifort, LLVM Flang, nvfortran, nagfor and LFortran
- [Diagnostics and dialects](diagnostics.md): zfls's own checks and their codes
- [The compiler check and linters](compiler-check.md): `compiler_diagnostics`, fortitude, Codee
- [Formatting and the source form](formatting.md): formatters, fixed and free form
- [Reading the source](source.md): comment markers, OpenMP and Intel conditional compilation, debug lines
- [Build files and C](build-files.md): `compile_commands.json`, `fpm.toml`, module files, `BIND(C)`
- [Running a file](running.md): `zfls/buildCommand` and `zfls build-command`
- [Debugging](debugging.md): `zfls dap` with gdb, lldb-dap or Windows's Debugger Engine
- [ifx without Visual Studio](ifx-kit.md): `zfls setup-ifx` and the ifx kit
- [fpm targets and tests](tests.md): `zfls/fpmTargets`, `zfls/fpmTests`, `zfls/pfunitTests`
- [Start-up time and memory](performance.md): the index cache, summaries
- [Differences from fortls](fortls.md)
